item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00234","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C15","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C09 is a direct and material drafting template for the later Citizenship Day proclamation. The child adapts the same citizenship observance to a newly designated date and statutory name while retaining C09's distinctive operative appeal to Federal, State, and local officials and interested organizations, its call for appropriate ceremonies involving all the people, and its stated goal that native-born/naturalized or old/new citizens better understand their rights, privileges, obligations, and responsibilities. C15 also plausibly contributed the flag-display and rights-and-responsibilities language, but C09 supplies the core structure and most distinctive wording.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I also urge Federal, State, and local officials, as well as patriotic, religious, civic, educational, and other interested organizations to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day in which all our people may join","parent_excerpt":"I also urge Federal, State, and local officials, as well as patriotic, civic, educational, and other interested organizations, to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on or about May 20 in which all our people may join","explanation":"This is a close, distinctive match in the enumeration of officials and organizations, the requested action, and the public-participation clause."},{"child_excerpt":"to the end that both native-born and naturalized citizens may have a fuller understanding of their rights and privileges and of their obligations and responsibilities as citizens of the United States","parent_excerpt":"to the end that both old and new citizens may have a fuller understanding of their rights and privileges and of their obligations and responsibilities as citizens","explanation":"The child preserves nearly the entire purpose clause, changing only the paired categories of citizens and adding 'of the United States.'"},{"child_excerpt":"all who, by coming of age or by naturalization, have attained the full status of citizenship","parent_excerpt":"those of our youth who have attained their majority and of those foreign-born who have become citizens through naturalization during the past year","explanation":"Both identify the commemorated class through the same two routes to newly attained citizenship status: coming of age and naturalization."}]}
